hypotheses.observation: Full producer-consumer fusion combines a 16 MiB single-use intermediate with severe resource costs: 224 registers per thread, 18.0 GB/s local spill, and 0.125 occupancy versus 0.62 when separate.
hypotheses.mechanism: The fused kernel's register pressure and spilling reduce resident warps and may outweigh savings from eliminating a kernel boundary and intermediate materialization.
hypotheses.transformation: Defer or reject full fusion; retain separate producer and consumer kernels pending end-to-end evidence.
preconditions: The measured fused resource usage is representative of the target workload and launch configuration.
The launch and intermediate-transfer costs are not dominant in total runtime.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Preserving the boundary is likely to avoid the fused kernel's occupancy and spill penalties, at the cost of the 0.003 ms launch and intermediate handling.
risks: Separate execution retains intermediate-memory traffic and another kernel launch.
The fused kernel could still win for sufficiently small workloads or if intermediate-transfer cost dominates.
unknowns: End-to-end runtime and speedup of separate versus fused execution.
Intermediate read/write bandwidth and whether it is a bottleneck.
Whether the fused resource usage can be reduced without changing the computation materially.
required_evidence: Measure end-to-end runtime for separate and fused versions on representative workloads.
Measure intermediate memory traffic, achieved bandwidth, and stall reasons.
Measure fused performance across relevant launch configurations and problem sizes.

hypotheses.observation: The consumer revisits its own tile four times, while the producer output is not reused after the consumer.
hypotheses.mechanism: The consumer has potential intra-tile locality, but fusion provides limited producer-output reuse because the intermediate is consumed only once.
hypotheses.transformation: Investigate consumer-side tile reuse or locality improvements while preserving the producer-consumer boundary; treat producer-output fusion benefit as uncertain.
preconditions: The four consumer tile revisits currently incur material cache or shared-memory misses.
The consumer's tile reuse can be improved without increasing register pressure or spills materially.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Improving consumer locality could reduce repeated tile data movement without incurring the full-fusion occupancy collapse.
risks: The tile may already reside effectively in cache or shared memory.
Additional staging could increase shared-memory use, synchronization, or registers.
unknowns: Current cache/shared-memory hit rates for the four tile revisits.
Whether consumer tile movement, rather than producer-output materialization, limits runtime.
required_evidence: Profile consumer-only cache/shared-memory behavior across the four revisits.
Compare consumer-only variants with measured registers, spills, occupancy, and runtime.
Measure whether intermediate traffic or consumer tile traffic dominates memory activity.

hypotheses.observation: The intermediate uses an independent accumulation order and requires tolerance validation.
hypotheses.mechanism: Any fusion or reassociation that changes execution order may alter numerical results, so performance comparisons must include numerical validation.
hypotheses.transformation: Use a numerically validated comparison of separate execution, full fusion, and any selective/tiled fusion candidate before considering the transformation viable.
preconditions: A defined tolerance and representative validation set are available.
The candidate preserves required output accuracy despite changed accumulation order.
hypotheses.expected_effect: This can distinguish genuine performance gains from transformations that are unacceptable due to numerical error, while preserving the option to defer uncertain fusion.
risks: Fusion or altered tiling may exceed tolerance.
Validation may expose input-dependent numerical failures not visible in a small test set.
unknowns: The actual tolerance threshold and validation coverage.
Whether separate and fused results differ materially on representative inputs.
Whether selective fusion changes accumulation order less than full fusion.
required_evidence: Run representative numerical tolerance validation for each candidate.
Measure runtime only for candidates that pass correctness validation.
Characterize error across input ranges and problem sizes.
